new_scholarship.name: University of Ljubljana Tuition Fee Exemption for International Students
new_scholarship.duration: No fixed award term is published. The exemption holds for the duration of the student's full-time study for as long as the exemption conditions continue to be met, and is carried forward through enrolment each academic year rather than granted for a set number of years.
new_scholarship.deadline: No application deadline is published. The University states the exemption for "full-time bachelor's and master's studies" as a standing rule and publishes no application window, no closing date and no separate scholarship call for it.
new_scholarship.application_period: No application period. There is no application window to open or close: the exemption is a standing tuition rule applied in the ordinary course of enrolment into full-time study, and the University publishes only a current price list, republished each academic year.
new_scholarship.application_method: Automatic on enrolment — there is no separate application. The University publishes who is exempt from paying tuition fees and who is obliged to pay; the exemption is settled through the enrolment process at the University of Ljubljana member institution (faculty or academy) in which the student enrols, and no scholarship application form or selection round exists for it.
new_scholarship.description: The University of Ljubljana publishes a standing tuition-fee exemption rather than an open international scholarship competition. Full-time bachelor's and master's study is fee-free for Slovenians (including Slovenians abroad and persons without Slovenian citizenship as defined by Slovenian law), citizens of EU countries plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia under bilateral education agreements with the Republic of Slovenia, permanent residents of the Republic of Slovenia who are taxpayers, persons granted international protection or under temporary protection, holders of Republic of Slovenia scholarships (CMEPIUS, JŠRIPSRS) and exchange students. Citizens of non-EU countries with which Slovenia has no bilateral agreement are explicitly listed as obliged to pay, as are all part-time students. The exemption removes the tuition fee only; enrolment fees and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation and living costs are not covered. The University also publishes two schemes of its own for international students, the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak and the Heart UL campaign, neither of which is a tuition scholarship.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Full-time applicants who already hold a nationality or residence status that the University lists as fee-exempt, chiefly nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia, EU/EEA-plus citizens studying in Slovenia, permanent residents of Slovenia who are tax residents, and holders of international or temporary protection. Not suitable as a funding route for a full-fee-paying non-EEA applicant, and not suitable for part-time study, which the University lists among those who must pay.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Eligibility is decided by nationality, residence status and study mode, not by academic merit or competition. The University states that no tuition fees are payable for full-time bachelor's and master's studies by Slovenians (including those living outside Slovenia and those without Slovenian citizenship as defined by the relevant law), students from EU countries together with Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, students from countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has concluded a bilateral agreement (Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia), students with permanent residence in the Republic of Slovenia who themselves or their parents/guardians are taxpayers of the Republic of Slovenia, persons granted international protection and persons under temporary protection, scholarship holders of the Republic of Slovenia (CMEPIUS, Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia), and exchange students including doctoral exchange students. The University states that tuition fees are paid by citizens of non-EU countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has not signed a bilateral agreement, by all students with an already acquired equivalent degree, by exempt students who change study programme or direction and enrol in the same or a lower study year after having exercised the right to repeat a year, by exempt students who re-enrol in the same study programme or direction from which they previously withdrew, by all part-time students, and by all doctoral students. No field or faculty restriction applies to the exemption, although the fee amount itself is published per member institution.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: There is no selection process. The University publishes the exemption as a standing fee rule decided by nationality, residence status, protection status, prior degree and study mode, and publishes no criteria, ranking, weighting or shortlist. The exemption is therefore not an award an applicant competes for.
new_scholarship.notes: SCOPE CORRECTION, stated plainly because the assigned award name was wrong. The b46 assignment row names a 'Jasminka Scholarship - University of Ljubljana'. No award of that name exists on the University of Ljubljana site. The University's own English scholarships page (https://www.uni-lj.si/en/study/scholarships, fetched 2026-10-03) lists only two University-run schemes for international students, the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak (a 4.5-month artist/designer/restorer residency, not a degree scholarship) and the Heart UL campaign (fundraising for enrolled students in financial emergency, not a tuition scholarship), and it refers all state scholarships for international students to the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia at srips-rs.si. 'Jasminka' is most plausibly a machine-generated garbling of the Fund's Slovenian name, Javni stipendijski, razvojni, invalidski in prezivninski sklad Republike Slovenije; that Fund is a different awarding body, so recording its Zois scholarships or its nationality-locked open calls (Western Balkans, Senegal/Nepal/East Timor, Angola, Ethiopia/Uganda/Rwanda, Türkiye refugees, Palestinian nationals) as a University of Ljubljana award would be a provenance error, and several of those calls are master's-only or locked to nationalities in excluded regions. This record therefore covers the only broad bachelor's-level funding instrument the University itself publishes: the statutory tuition-fee exemption for international students. It is a TUITION REDUCTION, not a scholarship: it is automatic on enrolment, has no application, no deadline, no competition, no stipend and no cash amount, and it applies only to the tuition fee. funding_amount is null on purpose: the University publishes the 2026/2027 tuition and study-contribution amounts as one PDF price list per faculty/academy plus separate lists for enrolment fees and study contributions, doctoral study and interdisciplinary bachelor programmes, and those PDFs were not opened for this record, so no EUR figure is recorded rather than inventing one. Those per-faculty tables mean the fee waived is field-specific in value, but the exemption itself is not restricted by field or faculty. No bond, service obligation or repayment clause is published; the exemption is a fee rule, and the conditions that can withdraw it (changing programme and enrolling in the same or a lower year after a repeat year, or re-enrolling in a programme previously withdrawn from) are recorded as award_holder_conditions. The same exemption rule covers full-time master's study; only the bachelor's level is recorded in degree_levels, and the doctoral level is explicitly excluded because the University lists all doctoral students as obliged to pay. Two official pages and the logo asset were fetched in total; no page was unreachable, but the per-faculty price-list PDFs, the Call for Enrolment for non-EU nationals, the international-students cost-of-living page and the Heart UL FAQ were not fetched, so amounts, enrolment deadlines and English-language requirements are recorded as null rather than guessed.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: Not an application cycle. The exemption is a standing rule for full-time study, and the University republishes the exemption conditions and the tuition and study-contribution price lists each academic year; the price lists on the page are for academic year 2026/2027.
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: No application deadline is published. The University states the exemption applies to "full-time bachelor's and master's studies" and publishes no opening date, closing date or call for applications for it.
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: There is no application window to record, so deadline_central, deadline_central_timezone and deadline_institutional are all null. The exemption is not applied for on a deadline; it is settled when the student enrols in full-time study, and the University publishes the rule rather than a call. Enrolment deadlines for foreign nationals from non-EU member states exist as a separate published Call for Enrolment, but that call governs admission, not this exemption, and it was not fetched, so no date and no timezone are claimed. Any such University of Ljubljana deadline would fall in Europe/Ljubljana time, but no published time was read, so the field stays null.
programme_detail_official.status_note: Continuously in force for full-time study; the University published the current conditions and the 2026/2027 price lists at the time of verification on 2026-10-03. There is no open or closed window because there is no application. The exemption is periodically revised by statute and the fee amounts are reissued every academic year, so the status refers to the standing rule, not to a cycle that can close.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: For the duration of the student's full-time study for as long as the exemption conditions are met, carried forward through enrolment each academic year; the University publishes no fixed award term.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: Covers the tuition fee in full for full-time bachelor's and master's study, and nothing else. It does not cover enrolment fees and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation, living costs, study materials or travel, and it carries no cash payment. The University lists all part-time students among those obliged to pay tuition fees, so the exemption is void for part-time enrolment. It is also lost by exempt students who change study programme or direction and enrol in the same or a lower study year after already having exercised the right to repeat a year, and by exempt students who re-enrol in the same study programme or direction from which they previously withdrew, as both groups are expressly listed as obliged to pay. Because the award is tuition-only and leaves the remaining components of the cost of study payable, fully_funded is false.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Full tuition fee waived for full-time study; enrolment fees and study contributions, health insurance, accommodation and living costs all remain payable by the student. No stipend, no cash amount, no bond or service obligation.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Determined by nationality, residence status and protection status rather than by merit. The University lists Slovenians (including those abroad and those without Slovenian citizenship as defined by the relevant law), citizens of EU countries plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia under bilateral education agreements, permanent residents of the Republic of Slovenia who are taxpayers of the Republic of Slovenia, persons granted international protection and persons under temporary protection, Republic of Slovenia scholarship holders and exchange students. Citizens of non-EU countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has not signed a bilateral agreement are expressly listed as obliged to pay.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: For the group this record is aimed at, the University publishes no open international scholarship competition: the only international schemes it runs are the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak, a 4.5-month residency for artists, designers, restorers, theorists and researchers from around the world, and the Heart UL campaign for enrolled students in financial emergency, neither of which funds a bachelor's degree's tuition. Non-EEA nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia qualify for the tuition exemption through a bilateral education agreement with the Republic of Slovenia, and persons granted international protection or under temporary protection qualify irrespective of nationality; all other non-EEA nationals are listed as paying. Scholarships linked from the University's page for international students, such as the Zois scholarships and the various open calls, are awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia and are not University of Ljubljana awards.
programme_detail_official.study_mode: Full-time only; the University lists all part-time students among those obliged to pay tuition fees.
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field, subject or faculty restriction on the exemption itself. The amount is field-specific: the University publishes one 2026/2027 price list per member institution (Academy of Fine Arts and Design, Academy of Music, Academy of Theatre Radio Film and Television, Biotechnical Faculty, Faculty of Architecture, Arts, Chemistry and Chemical Technology, Civil and Geodetic Engineering, Computer and Information Science, Education, Electrical Engineering, Health Sciences, Law, Maritime Studies and Transport, Mathematics and Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Medicine, Natural Sciences and Engineering, Pharmacy, Public Administration, Social Sciences, Social Work, Sport, Theology, School of Economics and Business and Veterinary Faculty), plus a separate price list for enrolment fees and study contributions, a separate list for interdisciplinary bachelor degree programmes, a separate list for interdisciplinary and joint master's programmes, a separate doctoral tuition list and a separate set of general conditions for the payment of tuition fees. Doctoral study is explicitly outside the exemption.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Automatic on enrolment. The University publishes the exemption as a standing fee rule, so there is no separate application, no application form, no call and no selection process; the exemption is applied in the ordinary course of enrolment.
programme_detail_official.application_route: No separate application route. The exemption is applied for in the course of enrolling in full-time study at the University of Ljubljana member institution in which the student studies, under the rules published on the University tuition fees page; the University's Higher Education Application and Information Service handles enrolment.

selection_criteria: No selection criteria. The exemption is a standing tuition-fee rule applied by nationality, residence status, protection status, prior degree and study mode, not a competitive award, and the University publishes no shortlist, ranking or interview.
programme_detail_official.duration: Duration of the student's full-time study, for as long as the exemption conditions are met; the University publishes no fixed award term for the exemption.

supplements_or_initiatives: Heart UL: a University of Ljubljana campaign whose stated aim is to raise funds for students who, due to special personal circumstances, find themselves in a financial emergency and consequently have no means of survival. It is a social-assistance campaign for enrolled students, not a tuition scholarship, and the University publishes no amount for it on the scholarships page.

Residency of Prof. Grega Košak: a University of Ljubljana residency of four and a half months in an apartment in the centre of Ljubljana for artists, designers, restorers, theorists and researchers from around the world. It is a residency, not a degree scholarship, and does not fund a bachelor's programme.

State scholarships for international students listed on the University page, including Zois scholarships and various open calls, are administered and awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia (srips-rs.si), not by the University; the University states that the Fund publishes the open call defining all requirements, procedures and the amount of scholarship grants.
Republic of Slovenia scholarship holders, including CMEPIUS holders, are listed by the University as exempt from tuition fees, so a state scholarship can also remove the tuition fee for the holder.

programme_detail_official.description: A statutory tuition-fee exemption applied by the University of Ljubljana, not a competitive scholarship. Full-time bachelor's and master's study is fee-free for Slovenians (including Slovenians abroad and persons without Slovenian citizenship as defined by the relevant law), citizens of EU countries plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia under bilateral education agreements, permanent residents of the Republic of Slovenia who are taxpayers, persons granted international protection or under temporary protection, Republic of Slovenia scholarship holders and exchange students. Citizens of non-EU countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has not signed a bilateral agreement, all part-time students, all doctoral students and all students holding an equivalent degree are obliged to pay. There is no application, no deadline, no competition, no stipend and no bond, and only the tuition fee is removed: enrolment fees and study contributions, health insurance, accommodation and living costs stay payable, so the award is not fully funded.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Tuition fee only, for full-time study, until the exemption conditions cease to apply. Enrolment fees and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation, living costs, study materials and travel are all outside the coverage.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality or residence status appears in the University's fee-exempt list before you rely on this: EU plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway; Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia; permanent residence in Slovenia with tax residency; or international or temporary protection.
If you are a citizen of a non-EU country with no bilateral agreement with Slovenia, stop here: the University lists you among those obliged to pay, and this exemption is not available to you.
Enrol in full-time study only. Part-time enrolment puts you in the group the University lists as obliged to pay, and the exemption will not be applied.
Check you do not already hold an equivalent degree of education, which also puts you in the paying group.
Budget separately for everything the exemption does not touch: enrolment fee and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation and living costs, study materials and travel.
Open the price list for your own faculty or academy for the relevant academic year, rather than assuming the fee is the same across the University, and use that figure in your funding plan.

If you are changing study programme or direction, or re-enrolling in a programme you previously left, raise it with the enrolling faculty before enrolling, because both situations are listed as forfeiting the exemption.
Contact the University or the enrolling member institution in writing to have your exemption status confirmed for your specific nationality and residence combination before you commit funds.
If you already hold a Republic of Slovenia scholarship such as CMEPIUS or a JŠRIPSRS award, tell the enrolling institution, as scholarship holders are listed as fee-exempt.

Consider the Fund's separate state scholarship routes for non-EEA nationals, but note those are awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia and are outside this record
common_rejection_risks: Assuming this is an open scholarship anyone can apply for. It is a standing fee rule, so there is no application to submit and no outcome to be rejected from; if your nationality is not on the exempt list, the fee simply applies.
Enrolling part-time and losing the exemption without realising it, because the University lists all part-time students as obliged to pay.
Already holding an equivalent degree and therefore being liable for the full fee.
Changing study programme or direction and enrolling in the same or a lower study year after having repeated a year, which the University lists as forfeiting the exemption.
Re-enrolling in the same study programme or direction previously withdrawn from, which the University also lists as forfeiting the exemption.
Assuming the Western Balkans agreement extends to all non-EEA countries. The University names Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia only.
Treating the exemption as fully funding the degree and being caught short on living costs in Ljubljana, which the fee waiver does nothing about.
Reading a third-party listing that calls this a 'Jasminka Scholarship'. No award of that name appears on the University of Ljubljana site.
Missing the annual change of fee tables and planning a budget from a previous academic year's per-faculty amount.
Assuming a state scholarship amount applies here. The Zois scholarships and the Fund's open calls named on the University page are awarded by the Fund, not the University.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs are the main gap. The exemption waives the tuition fee only and provides no stipend, so the full cost of living in Ljubljana, one of the more expensive capitals in the region, has to be met from other funds. No monthly figure is recorded in this record because the University's own cost-of-living guidance was not fetched; read the University international-students cost-of-living and accommodation pages, or your national scholarship body's published cost-of-living figure for Ljubljana, before budgeting.

Student dormitory rent or private rental, not covered. If you are not a Republic of Slovenia scholarship holder you do not have the subsidised scholarship-holder dormitory route described by the University, so expect the full foreign-student dormitory rate or market rent.
Compulsory health insurance for non-EU nationals, not covered by the fee exemption. Arrange it before the start of studies.

Enrolment fee and study contributions, charged separately from tuition and not covered, even where tuition is waived. Amounts are in the annual price list for enrolment fees and study contributions, which was not opened for this record.

Study materials, equipment and laboratory or fieldwork costs, depending on the faculty. The University's Heart UL campaign exists because enrolled students can face this kind of shortfall, which is why it is not safe to treat the fee waiver as complete funding.
Residence permit and visa costs, and health insurance required for the permit, for non-EU nationals.
Travel to and from Slovenia, which the exemption does not cover in either direction.

The tuition fee itself, for anyone outside the exempt categories, set per faculty and per study programme in the annual price lists. Those PDFs were not opened for this record, so no EUR figure is given here; use the figure for your own faculty.
Lost earnings or opportunity cost, which no fee exemption addresses and which applicants from outside the EEA should treat as a real component of the total cost.
document_audit: The University publishes no document checklist for this exemption, because there is no application. This list is derived guidance, not an official requirement.
Passport or other evidence of nationality, so the enrolling institution can check the fee-exempt nationality list, including the specific countries named under the bilateral agreements.

If you are a national of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo or Serbia, the evidence relied on is the bilateral education agreement with the Republic of Slovenia, so confirm with the enrolling institution that it accepts your nationality at face value for fee purposes.
Evidence of permanent residence in the Republic of Slovenia together with tax residency, for you or for your parents or guardians, if you are claiming exemption on that ground.
Evidence of international protection or of temporary protection, if you are claiming exemption on that ground.
Evidence of a Republic of Slovenia scholarship such as CMEPIUS or a JŠRIPSRS award, if you are claiming exemption as a scholarship holder.
Evidence of exchange status, if you are claiming exemption as an exchange student.
Confirm you have no previously awarded equivalent degree, which the University treats as a disqualifying condition for the exemption.
Keep your enrolment confirmation showing full-time status, since the exemption depends on it and is easiest to verify when the faculty can see it at enrolment.
Keep the fee assessment or invoice from your faculty showing the tuition line at zero, so a later change of programme or re-enrolment can be checked against what you were actually charged.

alerts.message: If you are a citizen of a non-EU country with which Slovenia has no bilateral agreement, the University lists you as obliged to pay tuition fees and this exemption does not apply to you. Do not build a funding plan on it.
All part-time students are listed as obliged to pay tuition fees. Only full-time enrolment qualifies for the exemption, so switching to part-time mid-programme can create an immediate fee liability.

Changing programme or direction and enrolling in the same or a lower study year after repeating a year, or re-enrolling in a programme you withdrew from, are both listed as forfeiting the exemption. Clear this with the faculty before enrolling.

The University republishes tuition and study-contribution price lists each academic year, with a separate list per faculty. Never plan from a previous year's figure, and always use the list for your own faculty and programme.

This is a tuition reduction applied automatically on enrolment. There is no application window, no deadline, no shortlist and no award letter to wait for, and there is no application to submit before you enrol.

No 'Jasminka Scholarship' exists at the University of Ljubljana. The University's scholarships page names only the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak, the Heart UL campaign and state scholarships awarded by the Fund at srips-rs.si.

The Zois scholarships and the open calls for foreign nationals linked from the University page are awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia. Check that Fund's own call for deadlines and amounts; they are not covered by this record and are frequently restricted by nationality or to master's level.

submission_workflow: No application exists for this exemption, so there is nothing to submit and no submission deadline to track.

Apply and enrol in full-time study through the ordinary University of Ljubljana admission and enrolment route for your nationality, which for non-EU nationals runs through the published Call for Enrolment and is handled by the Higher Education Application and Information Service at vpis@uni-lj.si.
At enrolment, present the evidence for your fee-exempt nationality, residence or protection status to the enrolling member institution so that the tuition line is assessed at zero.
Check the tuition and study-contribution invoice issued at enrolment and confirm the tuition line is zero and that the remaining enrolment fee and study contributions are as you budgeted.
If the tuition line is not zero, take it up with the enrolling faculty immediately with your exemption evidence, since the exemption is applied at that point rather than awarded later.
Re-confirm full-time status and exemption eligibility at each annual re-enrolment, because the exemption is carried forward through enrolment and is lost if the study mode or the programme changes.
Arrange compulsory health insurance before the start of studies, and separately arrange a residence permit, as neither is included in the fee exemption.
Apply for dormitory accommodation early through the University or the student dormitory, and budget the foreign-student rate if you are not a Republic of Slovenia scholarship holder.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The tuition fees page states the exemption for 'full-time bachelor's and master's studies' and, in the section on who is obliged to pay, names 'all doctoral students' and refers to repeat years 'at the same cycle of study', so the rule demonstrably reaches undergraduate degree study and excludes doctoral study. Bachelor's is the level recorded in new_scholarship.degree_levels; the master's level the same rule covers is noted in programme_detail_official.degree_levels and not presented as the record's level.
